grammar.note: Declines like dieser (solche, solches, solchen). In speech so ein is more common: so ein Wetter.
Colloquial. Mist! = Damn! So ein Mist! = What a pain! No plural in this sense.
jemandem böse sein = to be angry with someone (dative).
sich vorstellen = to introduce oneself; sich (dative) etwas vorstellen = to imagine: Ich kann mir das vorstellen.

example_source: May I [[introduce]] my wife to you?

grammar.note: wo(r)- + preposition asks about things: wovon, womit, worüber (reden von → wovon).
Subordinating: the verb goes to the end.

example_target: Ich rufe dich an, [[sobald]] ich zu Hause bin.
example_source: I’ll call you [[as soon as]] I’m home.

grammar.note: Colloquial short form of noch einmal.
No plural. For sex = gender use das Geschlecht.

example_target: Der Film zeigt keine Gewalt und keinen [[Sex]].
example_source: The film shows no violence and no [[sex]].

grammar.note: Mostly in wehtun (weh tun) with the dative: Das tut mir weh = That hurts me.
im Krankenhaus liegen = to be in hospital (as a patient).
A noun in German: eine Million, zwei Millionen.
Colloquial: Klasse! = Great!

example_source: Our [[class]] is going on a trip tomorrow.

grammar.note: Sinn haben / Sinn ergeben = to make sense; Sinn machen is common in speech.
At the start of a sentence the verb comes straight after it.
sich verletzen = to get hurt, to injure oneself.
sich ändern = to change (intransitive). Money: wechseln; clothes: sich umziehen.
Participle = infinitive. Also an adjective: erfahren = experienced.

example_source: How did you [[find out]] about it?

grammar.note: Vowel change in the present: du trägst, er trägt.

example_source: She [[is wearing]] a red dress today.

grammar.note: For numbers and amounts mindestens is more usual: mindestens zehn Euro.

example_target: Es regnet, aber [[wenigstens]] ist es warm.
example_source: It’s raining, but [[at least]] it’s warm.

grammar.note: stolz auf + accusative = proud of.

example_source: The coffee is too [[strong]] for me.

grammar.note: Vowel change: du fällst, er fällt. Perfekt with sein.

example_target: Das Glas ist auf den Boden [[gefallen]].

grammar.note: nicht besonders = not very, not particularly.
Always feminine, even for a man: Er ist eine nette Person.
Subordinating: the verb goes to the end. Written apart, so lange = for so long.

example_source: [[As long as]] it’s raining, we’re staying inside.

grammar.note: lachen über + accusative = to laugh at/about.
Takes a direct object, no preposition. ein Kind erwarten = to be expecting a baby.

example_source: The children are sitting on the [[floor]].

grammar.note: Colloquial; at work people usually say der Chef / die Chefin.

example_source: My [[boss]] is in a bad mood today.

grammar.note: stilles Wasser = still (non-sparkling) water.
The plural is only used in finance (collateral). mit Sicherheit = certainly.
kämpfen für / gegen / um + accusative.
Colloquial, no plural. Not to be confused with der Zeuge (witness).
lustig = amusing; komisch usually means strange.
Irregular like bringen (brachte, gebracht). Often figurative in speech.
Nicht schlimm! = Never mind, no problem.
Also as an intensifier: unglaublich teuer = incredibly expensive.

example_target: Der [[Laden]] macht um acht Uhr auf.

grammar.note: Ich bin der Meinung, dass … = I think that …
Feminine: die Mörderin.

example_target: Im Krimi findet die Polizei den [[Mörder]].
example_source: In the crime story the police find the [[murderer]].

grammar.note: Mostly used in the 3rd person; more formal than passieren. Perfekt with sein.
n-declension: den/dem Idioten. An insult, so use with care.
No plural. As a noun: forgiveness (um Verzeihung bitten = to apologise).
Perfekt with sein; with haben only when flying something: Sie hat das Flugzeug geflogen.

example_source: We’re [[flying]] to Spain in the summer.

grammar.note: Plural also die Generale.
An adverb; the conjunction "before" is bevor.
Schluss machen = to stop for the day / to break up. Plural = conclusions.

example_source: At the [[end]] of the film everyone cries.

example_target: Sie [[verdient]] in ihrem neuen Job gut.
example_source: She [[earns]] good money in her new job.

grammar.note: das Perfekt is also the name of the German present perfect tense.
jemandem (dative) etwas versprechen. sich versprechen = to make a slip of the tongue.

example_source: I [[promise]] you I’ll be on time.

grammar.note: False friend: handy = praktisch.
Opposite: vorne. nach hinten = to the back.

example_source: We’re sitting right [[at the back]] of the bus.

grammar.note: achtzehn = 18, achtzig = 80.
etwas nötig haben = to need something.

example_source: The crime novel is about a [[murder]].

grammar.note: Out towards the speaker (hinaus = away). Colloquially shortened to raus.
Also "outrageous" about behaviour: Du bist unmöglich!
Always masculine. Lieblings- = favourite: mein Lieblingsessen.
Also an adjective: actual, real.
Takes the dative. Perfekt with sein; in the sense "to obey" with haben.
jemanden um etwas bitten = to ask someone for something; for questions use fragen.

example_target: Darf ich Sie um einen Gefallen [[bitten]]?

grammar.note: Participle = infinitive. Vowel change: du behältst, er behält.
No plural. in der Nähe von + dative = near.

example_target: Gibt es hier in der [[Nähe]] eine Apotheke?

grammar.note: Also an adjective: ein plötzlicher Regen = a sudden shower.
Used in questions and negatives; je means the same.
mit etwas anfangen = to start (doing) something. Vowel change: du fängst an.

example_source: Our [[hotel]] is right on the beach.

grammar.note: Also a qualification: Meister = master craftsman. Feminine: die Meisterin.
Subordinating: the verb goes to the end.

example_source: [[Although]] it’s raining, we’re going for a walk.

grammar.note: siebzehn = 17, siebzig = 70 (no -en-).
Usually "strange"; for "funny = amusing" lustig is clearer.
etwas bezahlen = to pay for something (no preposition). No ge- in the participle.
No plural. Ärger bekommen/kriegen = to get into trouble.

example_target: Sonst bekommst du [[Ärger]] mit deinem Vater.
example_source: Otherwise you’ll get into [[trouble]] with your father.
The [[picture]] hangs in the living room.

grammar.note: Hast du etwas dagegen? = Do you mind? Also contrast: Er dagegen trinkt Kaffee.

example_source: In the crime novel a [[body]] is found.

grammar.note: verheiratet mit + dative = married to.
n-declension: den/dem Agenten. Feminine: die Agentin.

example_target: Er arbeitet als [[Agent]] für den Geheimdienst.
example_source: He works as an [[agent]] for the secret service.

example_target: Ich hatte heute Nacht einen komischen [[Traum]].
example_source: I had a strange [[dream]] last night.

grammar.note: eine Entscheidung treffen = to make a decision.
in der Regel = as a rule, usually.
Vowel change: du fängst, er fängt.
Means the same as weg, slightly more formal. und so fort = and so on.
Very often used as an adverb: constantly, all the time.

example_source: The child is out of [[danger]] now.

grammar.note: Bescheid sagen/geben = to let someone know; Bescheid wissen = to know about it. Plural only for official notices.

example_target: Sag mir bitte [[Bescheid]], wenn du da bist.
example_source: Please [[let me know]] when you’re there.

grammar.note: Often um … herum. Colloquially rum.
Irregular genitive des Gedankens; otherwise -n: den/dem Gedanken. sich Gedanken machen = to worry.
In southern Germany and Austria also benützen.
sich (dative) etwas wünschen = to wish for something: Ich wünsche mir ein Fahrrad.

example_target: Ich [[wünsche]] dir alles Gute zum Geburtstag!

grammar.note: In a restaurant: Zahlen, bitte! = The bill, please! Close in meaning to bezahlen.
Anfang + month without article; am Anfang = at the beginning.

example_source: We’re going on holiday at the [[beginning]] of May.

grammar.note: legen = to put down (flat), with accusative (wohin?); liegen = to lie, with dative (wo?).

example_target: Ich [[lege]] das Buch auf den Tisch.
example_source: I [[put]] the book on the table.

grammar.note: Feminine: die Anwältin.

example_source: I need to speak to my [[lawyer]].

grammar.note: Not to be confused with der Arm (arm). Du Armer! = You poor thing!

example_target: Viele Menschen in der Stadt sind [[arm]].
example_source: Many people in the city are [[poor]].

grammar.note: Feminine: die Partnerin.
Slang: Halt die Klappe! = Shut up! (rude).

example_source: The [[flap]] on the letterbox is stuck.

example_target: Ich habe mich in den [[Finger]] geschnitten.

grammar.note: The wedding itself is die Hochzeit.
Das spielt keine Rolle = It doesn’t matter.

example_source: She plays the [[role]] of the mother.

grammar.note: False friend: not "high time" (höchste Zeit).
wo(r)- + zu; asks about purpose.

example_source: [[What]] do you need the money for?

grammar.note: False friend: a chef (cook) is der Koch. Feminine: die Chefin.

example_target: Mein [[Chef]] ist heute nicht im Büro.
example_source: My [[boss]] isn’t in the office today.

grammar.note: Countable in German and often plural.
erledigt sein (colloquial) = to be worn out.

example_source: I still have a lot to [[get done]] today.

grammar.note: sich (dative) etwas ansehen = to watch / have a look at: Wir sehen uns einen Film an.

example_source: Why are you [[looking at]] me like that?
